previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for surgical management of malignant fibrous histiocytoma in the left tibia, diagnosed after an open biopsy following a non-diagnostic CT-guided procedure. She underwent wide excision of the tumor with intercalary prosthetic reconstruction and a medial gastrocnemius flap. The surgery was uncomplicated, and she recovered well with controlled pain, no signs of infection, and stable hemoglobin. She was transitioned to oral pain medications, advanced in physical therapy with weight-bearing as tolerated, and discharged home on postoperative day five. Discharge instructions included Lovenox for DVT prophylaxis, wound care, pain management, and follow-up with orthopedics and oncology.

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL INDICATION: Patient with osteosarcoma requiring double-lumen chest
port placement.
 
CLINICIANS: Dr. ___ and Dr. ___. The attending, Dr.
___,
was present and supervising throughout.
 
ANESTHESIA: 1% buffered lidocaine and lidocaine mixed with epinephrine was
used for local
anesthesia. Moderate conscious sedation was provided by administering 4 mg of
Versed and 200 mcg of fentanyl throughout the total intraservice time of 1
hour during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by a trained radiological nurse.
 
PROCEDURE:
1. Right internal jugular venous access.
2. Subcutaneous pocket creation over the right upper anterior chest wall.
3. Placement of a double-lumen chest port via the right IJV, left accessed as
requested.
 
PROCEDURE DETAIL: A written informed consent was obtained explaining the
risks and benefits of the procedure. The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table. A preprocedure
timeout and huddle was performed per ___ protocol.
 
The right side of the upper chest was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.
  
Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the right internal jugular vein which
was patent and compressible was accessed using a micropuncture needle, and an
018 
nitinol wire was passed into the SVC. The needle was
exchanged for a ___ micropuncture sheath and the wire for a short 035 ___
wire which
was used to make appropriate measurement for catheter length and then passed
distally into the IVC for stability..
 
Next, attention was turned towards creation of a subcutaneous pocket over the
right upper anterior chest wall. After instilling superficial and deeper
local anesthesia, a 2.5 cm transverse incision was made over the right upper
anterior chest wall, and a subcutaneous pocket was created by using blunt
dissection. The pocket was intermittently irrigated with normal saline
solution. The dual-lumen port was then connected to the catheter. The catheter
was then tunneled from the subcutaneous pocket towards the venotomy site from
where it was brought out using a tunneling device. The dual-lumen
port was then connected to the catheter, and checks were made for any leaks by
accessing the diaphragms using non-coring ___ needles. No leaks were found.
The port was then placed in the subcutaneous pocket and secured with ___
Prolene sutures on either side. The venotomy tract was dilated using the
introducer of the peelaway sheath supplied with the kit. Following this, the
peel-away sheath was placed over the ___ wire through which the catheter of
the port was threaded into the right side of the heart with tip in the right
atrium. The sheath was then peeled out. Before closure, the subcutaneous
pocket and the tunnel were
irrigated with normal saline.The subcutaneous pocket was closed
in layers using ___ subcutaneous interrupted and ___ subcuticular continuous
sutures. ___ subcuticular sutures were also used to close the venotomy
incision site.  
Steri-Strips were applied over the sutures.
Both the ports were accessed using non-coring ___ needles and could be
aspirated and flushed easily. an appropriate amount of heparin was instilled
into each port. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient withstood the
procedure well and had no immediate complications. Final spot fluoroscopic
image demonstrated good alignment of the port with the catheter with no acute
kinks. 
The tip terminates in the right atrium.
 
IMPRESSION: 
Uncomplicated placement of a right-sided double-lumen power injectable chest
port
via the right internal jugular venous approach. The tip of the catheter
terminates in the right atrium. Both the lumens are left accessed as per
request and the catheter is ready for use.
